_comment: The versioned marker list for slop-lint (REQ-02, ADR-1110). Every entry names a BAD pattern.
There is no entry here that requires anything of an article -- no minimum heading count, no
required section, no word floor. ADR-1110 makes that one-way: a prescriptive rule may be added
only by its own ADR that argues the creativity cost and names what it forbids the writer from
doing. Adding a positive rule to this file instead is the drift the ADR exists to prevent.
Markers are LITERAL phrases, not regexes, matched case-insensitively against a normalised
line. That is deliberate: this lane already shipped a ReDoS in titleToKeyword, and a marker
file that carries regexes turns every future edit to a reviewed data file into a way to hang
the linter. Morphology is handled by listing the variants, which is also easier to review --
a reader can see exactly what is caught without simulating a pattern in their head.
`structural` markers cannot be expressed as a phrase; each has code behind it in slop-lint.mjs
keyed by its id, and its threshold lives HERE so the code carries no tunable of its own.
WHAT THIS LIST CANNOT DO, stated here rather than discovered later: text that trips no marker
is not thereby good. A marker-free sample that is still slop PASSES, by construction -- that is
the honest-limit fixture in tests/growth-lints.bats, and the POV floor at the human gate is the

phrases.why: The single most reliable machine tell; no human reaches for it.
Inflated metaphor standing in for a concrete claim.
Says a field changes, which is true of every field.
Opening filler that dates nothing and locates nothing.
Asserts significance instead of showing it.
Metaphor for 'deal with' that carries no information.
Claims impact with no measurement behind it.
Claims an absence of friction that is never demonstrated.
Category words standing in for the thing itself.
Announces that a sentence is coming instead of writing it.
Essay-scaffolding connectives that a written argument does not need.
Four words that do the work of a preposition.
variants: at the end of the day
the fact of the matter is

phrases.why: The not-just-X-but-Y cadence, a machine rhythm rather than an argument.
Depth claimed by metaphor rather than by content.
Unfalsifiable praise with no source behind it.
Engagement bait; E3 forbids it outright (ADR-1111).

structural.why: Em-dash overuse is a strong machine tell. The threshold counts a LINE, not the document, so one dense sentence is caught rather than averaged away by a document-wide ratio.

_structural_note: Rule-of-three detection was DROPPED from v1 rather than shipped weak. Distinguishing a machine
cadence from a list of three real things needs the sentence's meaning, and every cheap
approximation flagged ordinary prose. A marker that fires on correct writing teaches the writer
to ignore the lint, which costs more than the pattern it was catching. It goes in when someone
has a test for it that a human agrees with.
